name: The ascent in yoga of BhG ch. 6

stages.name: ārurukṣu
stages.gloss: one wishing to ascend to yoga
stages.description: For the sage wishing to ascend to yoga, action (karma) is said to be the means (6.3); action done without depending on its fruit makes one renouncer and yogin (6.1); cf. yogins act, abandoning attachment, for self-purification (5.11).

stages.name: yogārūḍha
stages.gloss: one who has ascended to yoga
stages.description: For the same sage once ascended, calm (śama) is said to be the means (6.3); he is called ascended when he is attached neither to sense-objects nor to actions and has renounced all intentions (6.4).

stages.name: yuñjīta (constant practice of meditation)
stages.description: Constant meditation in solitude on a firm seat, the mind (manas) one-pointed and thought (citta) fixed on the Lord, with moderation in food and sleep; gradually stilling the mind and bringing it back when it wanders (6.10–17, 6.24–26).

stages.name: yukta
stages.description: When the well-restrained mind (citta) rests in the self alone, free of craving for all desires, one is called yoked; the mind is like a lamp in a windless place (6.18–19).

stages.name: yoga (duḥkha-saṃyoga-viyoga)
stages.description: The stilled mind (citta) comes to rest, the self is seen by the self, boundless happiness beyond the senses is known and one is unshaken by sorrow — the unyoking from union with sorrow (6.20–23).

stages.name: brahmabhūta / brahma-saṃsparśa
stages.description: The highest happiness comes to the calmed, stainless yogin who has become Brahman; he attains the boundless happiness of contact with Brahman (6.27–28).

stages.name: sarvatra samadarśana
stages.description: Seeing the self in all beings and all beings in the self, seeing the Lord everywhere, abiding in him however one lives; seeing pleasure and pain everywhere by likeness to oneself (6.29–32).

stages.name: parā gati / nirvāṇa-paramā śānti
stages.gloss: the highest goal; peace culminating in nirvāṇa
stages.description: The yogin always yoking himself attains the peace culminating in nirvāṇa that abides in the Lord (6.15); striving, cleansed, perfected over many births, he reaches the highest goal (6.45).

notes: Merged from extractor A (8 stages, this id) and extractor B (pth:bhagavad-gita-aruruksu-yogarudha: ārurukṣu → yogārūḍha → the highest peace). Only stages 1–2 are given by the text as an explicit sequence (6.3); stages 3–7 follow the chapter's order of description, not a numbered sequence (B recorded those states as phenomenology instead), and stage 8 is the chapter's own statement of the result. The chapter also says the ascent may span many births (6.41–45) and that of all yogins the faithful worshipper of the Lord is the most yoked (6.47). Band assignments are interpretive (interpretation layer).
